When the task meets ANY of the following, call orchestrate directly and automatically in the first turn — no explicit user request needed, and do not serially handle each item yourself (especially when reading or understanding a large project or codebase, do not start with sequential read/glob browsing): (1) it decomposes into 2+ independent subtasks (e.g. reading a large project, multi-file research, batch review, comparing options, multi-repo checks); (2) it needs staged progress (requirements → design → implementation plan); (3) it needs a senior review gate (code review, design review, QA); (4) it needs one suitable task routed from a candidate list. skill.body:
# dsh-ha-orchestrator usage & troubleshooting

## Capabilities

- Model high availability (HA): on request failure, models are quarantined (threshold/cooldown) and traffic fails over to backups; two-level circuits (model + provider), burst-window counting, real probe recovery, and optional context-window degradation.
- Orchestration: fanout / pipeline / supervisor (multiple reviewers + review rounds) / map-reduce / router; global concurrency, per-run subagent budgets, resume, presets, tool allow/deny, structured outputSchema, and delegation-depth limits. Unsupported provider capabilities are stripped before start.
- Research presets: built-in researcher and research-merger agents for multi-target research with official URLs, observation dates, preserved evidence, and explicit conflicts.
- Observability: /ha status|diag|reset|probe, /orchestrate runs|show <runId>|presets; JSONL run records plus one Markdown artifact per run containing full subtask output.

## Usage

1. Configure backups: use "Recommended backups" in the Model High Availability settings card, or fill provider/model manually; without backups there is no automatic failover.
2. Let the model orchestrate: just describe the task — the injected context guides the model to call the orchestrate tool automatically (fanout/pipeline/supervisor/map-reduce/router) when the task splits well.
3. Inspect runs: /orchestrate runs lists recent runs, /orchestrate show <runId> shows details; after an interruption, resume unfinished subtasks by runId via the orchestrate resume parameter.
4. Probe a model manually: /ha probe <provider> <model> verifies availability immediately (a quarantined model is released when the probe succeeds).
5. For a fixed output shape, add outputHint or an object-root outputSchema to a task; for review, use supervisor reviewers/reviewRounds.

## Troubleshooting

- No failover: check ha.enabled, non-empty backups, the codes error-code filter, and that the provider is registered in llm.listProviders.
- Model stays quarantined: /ha diag shows service availability and persistence state; failed probes extend cooldown (60s-5min), use /ha probe to verify manually.
- Structured output or tool filtering has no effect: confirm the provider declares the corresponding capability; unsupported fields are stripped before start so the subtask can still run.
- /ha or /orchestrate commands missing: deployments without the commands service skip commands automatically (rest of the plugin keeps working); /ha diag flags missing services.
- Config not applied: /ha diag shows configLoaded, haStateLoaded, and the persistence path; config lives in dsh-ha-orchestrator.config.json (plus .backup.json) and can be exported/imported from the System settings card.
